A couple of quick notes up front:
- The adapter supports mutual TLS and token-exchange (OIDC) for customer deployments.
- We have an optional local connector for air-gapped/on-prem customers; it holds a local cache of recent responses to reduce egress.
- Our default fallback is: primary model endpoint → lightweight local reranker → queued retry against secondary model variant.

Will bring the runbook and a sample network-fallback matrix to the call.

On Tue, May 19, 2026 at 10:40 AM Jin Park <jin.park@cleverops.io> wrote:
> We can do Thu 5/20 10:00 PT — that works for our engineering lead (Ava Kim) and our platform architect (Marco Ruiz).

Thanks — 10:00 PT on Thu works for Redwood team too. A few technical items I'd like to flag ahead of the call so we can get answers live: 

1) Network topology: do you support VPC peering, private link, and/or TLS mTLS? For private deployments we prefer VPC peering + SG-level controls.
2) Auth flow: describe token-exchange for short-lived tokens. Does the adapter use our standard OIDC flow or a separate key exchange? Example sequence would help (request → token exchange → upstream call).
3) Failure modes: list expected behavior for (a) downstream model timeout, (b) adapter internal crash, (c) network partition to the model cluster. For each case, please state what client sees (error code, retry-able vs not).
4) Model compatibility: which open model formats/architectures do you proxy (GGML, ONNX, hf transformers)? Any known constraints on sequence length or KV cache behavior?
5) Rate limiting and backpressure: how does the adapter surface downstream throttling? Any per-customer QPS limits or token-based throttles?
6) Observability: what traces/metrics/logs are available (span names, request ids) and can we push to our tracing backend?
7) Canary plan: sample test vectors (prompt sets), acceptance criteria (latency, 95p latency, error budget), rollback criteria.
8) Security/compliance: does the adapter persist logs or prompts, for how long, and are they encrypted at rest?

If you can include short sample payloads (JSON) and a small network-fallback matrix on the call, that will speed sign-off.

Cheers,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Integration Engineer | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Partner tech deep-dive: CleverOps adapter resilience & failover rubric

Sergio / team — good questions. Answers at a high level below; we will walk the details on the call and share the sample payloads and matrices.

1) Network topology: we support VPC peering (preferred for enterprise), private-link style endpoints, and mTLS for connector-to-adapter. For hosted integrations we support egress over TLS with IP allowlist.

2) Auth flow: adapter implements an OIDC token-exchange pattern. Typical sequence: client -> Redwood (short-lived token) -> adapter (exchanges for partner-scoped token via OIDC / token-introspect). We added a sample token-exchange payload (token-exchange-sample.json) in the Drive folder.

3) Failure modes:
- downstream model timeout: adapter returns HTTP 504; by default the client sees 504 and a retryable flag in the response body.
- adapter crash: if process restarts, active requests fail-fast with 503 and a clear retry-after header; we also emit an event to our webhook which you can subscribe to.
- network partition to model cluster: adapter falls back to a lightweight local reranker (if enabled) and returns a 200 with a best-effort result flagged as "degraded" in the metadata.

4) Model compatibility: we proxy HF transformer APIs and ONNX endpoints. GGML local connectors are supported via the on-prem connector but with reduced sequence-length (<= 2048) and no KV cache sharing.

5) Rate limiting/backpressure: adapter supports token-bucket per-customer rate limiting and dynamic throttling via a 429 with Retry-After; we also expose a backpressure header (X-Adapter-Queue-Length).

6) Observability: we export traces (OpenTelemetry), request_id header (X-Request-Id), span names prefixed with cleverops.adapter, and metrics (latency_token_ms, tokens_processed). We can ship a tracing shim to Redwood tracing backend — will coordinate with Aditya offline.

7) Canary plan suggestions: 48-hour sandbox; target 95p latency < 350ms for small model variants, error rate < 0.5%. Rollback if 95p > 700ms OR error rate > 2% sustained for 30 minutes. We'll bring the test vectors and network-fallback-matrix.xlsx to the call.

8) Security/compliance: persisted logs are configurable per-customer. Default retention is 7 days; encryption at rest is AES-256. We can enable strict zero-persist mode for regulated customers.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3CleVeRoPs-Integration (runbook, token sample, matrices)

We'll be on the 5/20 10:00 PT call and will open with the architecture.

— Jin
Jin Park
Head of Partnerships | CleverOps
